The 1-second end tolerance ÔÇö reproduced, and one thing the owner has not ruled\n\nReproduction on the r1 bytes, window `[15:00, 18:00)`, the real `18:00:00.060Z` stamp:\n\n| Stamp | Observed |\n|---|---|\n| `18:00:00.060Z` (the captured one, +0.060 s) | **accepted**, `REAL_CAPTURE_CANDIDATE_BUILT` |\n| +0.999 s | accepted |\n| **+1.000 s** | **refused** `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n| +1.060 s | refused `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n\n`end_limit = (end.seconds + 1, end.fraction)` with a strict `<` (`:1607`, `:1614`), so the admitted band is the half-open `[end, end+1 s)`. A stamp at exactly one second past the end is refused. The owner wrote \"a 1-second end-boundary tolerance\"; half-open is a defensible reading, but the boundary itself was chosen by the implementation, not by the row. ÔåÆ **NIT-2**.\n\n**The grid.** For `[15:00, 18:00)` the grid is `range(start, end+1h, 1h)` = `15, 16, 17, 18` (`:1237`) ÔÇö both endpoints inclusive. Combined with `position_at(hour)` using the position held *before* that hour (`:1222-1235`, `fill_ms < time_ms`), the grid is consistent with the venue's convention that the payment stamped at hour *H* settles `[HÔêÆ1h, H)`. Including the end hour is exactly what the owner's tolerance is for, and I confirm it is the same one second, not a second mechanism.\n\n**The start side is NOT stated anywhere, and it is not the owner's decision.** I searched all four files for any statement of which accrual interval a payment settles: the only occurrence is a test docstring, `tests/test_mtc_funding_export_real_capture.py:744` (\"the 18:00:00.060Z payment settles the 17-18 interval\"). Nothing in the exporter, the adapter, the candidate artifact or the report says it. I built the demonstrating case (position already open at the window start, payments at 15/16/17/18):\n\n```\neffective_interval : {'start_inclusive': '2026-09-14T15:00:00Z', 'end_exclusive': '2026-09-14T19:00:00Z', 'end_tolerance_seconds': 1}\ncompletion_check   : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']   (expected_funding_hours)\ninterval_hour_utc  : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']\n```\n\nA candidate that declares the interval `[15:00, 19:00)` therefore witnesses the accrual intervals `[14:00,15:00) ÔÇĞ [17:00,18:00)` ÔÇö i.e. the accrual coverage is `[start ÔêÆ 1 h, end)`: the declared window **plus one hour before its declared start**. The start hour is mandatory, not optional: deleting the 15:00 payment from that same capture refuses with \"expects payments at [15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00] ÔÇĞ carry payments at [16:00, 17:00, 18:00]\".\n\nTwo consequences the roster and the owner should see (neither is a fence hole ÔÇö both fail toward refusal ÔÇö so neither blocks this candidate):\n\n1. `interval_hour_utc` and `effective_interval` name a **payment-stamp** window while reading as an accrual window, and the witness silently reaches one hour before the declared start. Under D-3 the owner ruled the *value* (the floor of the stamp); the *meaning* of the window relative to accrual is unruled and stated nowhere in the artifacts. It needs one owner sentence. ÔåÆ **NIT-6**.\n2. On the end side this interacts with the capture tool. r1's manifest requests `userFunding` with `endTime = 1789412400000` (= `19:00:00.000Z`), while the exporter's grid expects a payment at `19:00` whenever the position is still open then ÔÇö and that payment is stamped 41-60 ms *past* the hour, outside the capture request bounds. My D-6 (iv) mutant is exactly this case and refuses. So a real capture whose window does not end flat is, as built, structurally un-witnessable: the exporter applies the tolerance, the capture request does not. The failure is conservative (refusal, never admission), but the accepting half cannot witness the general case today. The 1-second end tolerance ÔÇö reproduced, and one thing the owner has not ruled\n\nReproduction on the r1 bytes, window `[15:00, 18:00)`, the real `18:00:00.060Z` stamp:\n\n| Stamp | Observed |\n|---|---|\n| `18:00:00.060Z` (the captured one, +0.060 s) | **accepted**, `REAL_CAPTURE_CANDIDATE_BUILT` |\n| +0.999 s | accepted |\n| **+1.000 s** | **refused** `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n| +1.060 s | refused `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n\n`end_limit = (end.seconds + 1, end.fraction)` with a strict `<` (`:1607`, `:1614`), so the admitted band is the half-open `[end, end+1 s)`. A stamp at exactly one second past the end is refused. The owner wrote \"a 1-second end-boundary tolerance\"; half-open is a defensible reading, but the boundary itself was chosen by the implementation, not by the row. ÔåÆ **NIT-2**.\n\n**The grid.** For `[15:00, 18:00)` the grid is `range(start, end+1h, 1h)` = `15, 16, 17, 18` (`:1237`) ÔÇö both endpoints inclusive. Combined with `position_at(hour)` using the position held *before* that hour (`:1222-1235`, `fill_ms < time_ms`), the grid is consistent with the venue's convention that the payment stamped at hour *H* settles `[HÔêÆ1h, H)`. Including the end hour is exactly what the owner's tolerance is for, and I confirm it is the same one second, not a second mechanism.\n\n**The start side is NOT stated anywhere, and it is not the owner's decision.** I searched all four files for any statement of which accrual interval a payment settles: the only occurrence is a test docstring, `tests/test_mtc_funding_export_real_capture.py:744` (\"the 18:00:00.060Z payment settles the 17-18 interval\"). Nothing in the exporter, the adapter, the candidate artifact or the report says it. I built the demonstrating case (position already open at the window start, payments at 15/16/17/18):\n\n```\neffective_interval : {'start_inclusive': '2026-09-14T15:00:00Z', 'end_exclusive': '2026-09-14T19:00:00Z', 'end_tolerance_seconds': 1}\ncompletion_check   : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']   (expected_funding_hours)\ninterval_hour_utc  : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']\n```\n\nA candidate that declares the interval `[15:00, 19:00)` therefore witnesses the accrual intervals `[14:00,15:00) ÔÇĞ [17:00,18:00)` ÔÇö i.e. the accrual coverage is `[start ÔêÆ 1 h, end)`: the declared window **plus one hour before its declared start**. The start hour is mandatory, not optional: deleting the 15:00 payment from that same capture refuses with \"expects payments at [15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00] ÔÇĞ carry payments at [16:00, 17:00, 18:00]\".\n\nTwo consequences the roster and the owner should see (neither is a fence hole ÔÇö both fail toward refusal ÔÇö so neither blocks this candidate):\n\n1. `interval_hour_utc` and `effective_interval` name a **payment-stamp** window while reading as an accrual window, and the witness silently reaches one hour before the declared start. ÔåÆ **NIT-6**.\n2. The 1-second end tolerance ÔÇö reproduced, and one thing the owner has not ruled\n\nReproduction on the r1 bytes, window `[15:00, 18:00)`, the real `18:00:00.060Z` stamp:\n\n| Stamp | Observed |\n|---|---|\n| `18:00:00.060Z` (the captured one, +0.060 s) | **accepted**, `REAL_CAPTURE_CANDIDATE_BUILT` |\n| +0.999 s | accepted |\n| **+1.000 s** | **refused** `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n| +1.060 s | refused `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n\n`end_limit = (end.seconds + 1, end.fraction)` with a strict `<` (`:1607`, `:1614`), so the admitted band is the half-open `[end, end+1 s)`. A stamp at exactly one second past the end is refused. The owner wrote \"a 1-second end-boundary tolerance\"; half-open is a defensible reading, but the boundary itself was chosen by the implementation, not by the row. ÔåÆ **NIT-2**.\n\n**The grid.** For `[15:00, 18:00)` the grid is `range(start, end+1h, 1h)` = `15, 16, 17, 18` (`:1237`) ÔÇö both endpoints inclusive. Combined with `position_at(hour)` using the position held *before* that hour (`:1222-1235`, `fill_ms < time_ms`), the grid is consistent with the venue's convention that the payment stamped at hour *H* settles `[HÔêÆ1h, H)`. Including the end hour is exactly what the owner's tolerance is for, and I confirm it is the same one second, not a second mechanism.\n\n**The start side is NOT stated anywhere, and it is not the owner's decision.** I searched all four files for any statement of which accrual interval a payment settles: the only occurrence is a test docstring, `tests/test_mtc_funding_export_real_capture.py:744` (\"the 18:00:00.060Z payment settles the 17-18 interval\"). Nothing in the exporter, the adapter, the candidate artifact or the report says it. I built the demonstrating case (position already open at the window start, payments at 15/16/17/18):\n\n```\neffective_interval : {'start_inclusive': '2026-09-14T15:00:00Z', 'end_exclusive': '2026-09-14T19:00:00Z', 'end_tolerance_seconds': 1}\ncompletion_check   : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']   (expected_funding_hours)\ninterval_hour_utc  : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']\n```\n\nA candidate that declares the interval `[15:00, 19:00)` therefore witnesses the accrual intervals `[14:00,15:00) ÔÇĞ [17:00,18:00)` ÔÇö i.e. the accrual coverage is `[start ÔêÆ 1 h, end)`: the declared window **plus one hour before its declared start**. The start hour is mandatory, not optional: deleting the 15:00 payment from that same capture refuses with \"expects payments at [15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00] ÔÇĞ carry payments at [16:00, 17:00, 18:00]\".\n\nTwo consequences the roster and the owner should see (neither is a fence hole ÔÇö both fail toward refusal ÔÇö so neither blocks this candidate):\n\n1. `interval_hour_utc` and `effective_interval` name a **payment-stamp** window while reading as an accrual window, and the witness silently reaches one hour before the declared start. Under D-3 the owner ruled the *value* (the floor of the stamp); the *meaning* of the window relative to accrual is unruled and stated nowhere in the artifacts. It needs one owner sentence. ÔåÆ **NIT-6**.\n2. On the end side this interacts with the capture tool. r1's manifest requests `userFunding` with `endTime = 1789412400000` (= `19:00:00.000Z`), while the exporter's grid expects a payment at `19:00` whenever the position is still open then ÔÇö and that payment is stamped 41-60 ms *past* the hour, outside the capture request bounds. My D-6 (iv) mutant is exactly this case and refuses. So a real capture whose window does not end flat is, as built, structurally un-witnessable: the exporter applies the tolerance, the capture request does not. The failure is conservative (refusal, never admission), but the accepting half cannot witness the general case today. ÔåÆ **NIT-6** (same recommendation: state the semantics, and extend the capture request past the tolerance before the next capture is run).\n\n## 4. The 1-second end tolerance ÔÇö reproduced, and one thing the owner has not ruled\n\nReproduction on the r1 bytes, window `[15:00, 18:00)`, the real `18:00:00.060Z` stamp:\n\n| Stamp | Observed |\n|---|---|\n| `18:00:00.060Z` (the captured one, +0.060 s) | **accepted**, `REAL_CAPTURE_CANDIDATE_BUILT` |\n| +0.999 s | accepted |\n| **+1.000 s** | **refused** `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n| +1.060 s | refused `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n\n`end_limit = (end.seconds + 1, end.fraction)` with a strict `<` (`:1607`, `:1614`), so the admitted band is the half-open `[end, end+1 s)`. A stamp at exactly one second past the end is refused. The owner wrote \"a 1-second end-boundary tolerance\"; half-open is a defensible reading, but the boundary itself was chosen by the implementation, not by the row. ÔåÆ **NIT-2**.\n\n**The grid.** For `[15:00, 18:00)` the grid is `range(start, end+1h, 1h)` = `15, 16, 17, 18` (`:1237`) ÔÇö both endpoints inclusive. Combined with `position_at(hour)` using the position held *before* that hour (`:1222-1235`, `fill_ms < time_ms`), the grid is consistent with the venue's convention that the payment stamped at hour *H* settles `[HÔêÆ1h, H)`. Including the end hour is exactly what the owner's tolerance is for, and I confirm it is the same one second, not a second mechanism.\n\n**The start side is NOT stated anywhere, and it is not the owner's decision.** I searched all four files for any statement of which accrual interval a payment settles: the only occurrence is a test docstring, `tests/test_mtc_funding_export_real_capture.py:744` (\"the 18:00:00.060Z payment settles the 17-18 interval\"). Nothing in the exporter, the adapter, the candidate artifact or the report says it. I built the demonstrating case (position already open at the window start, payments at 15/16/17/18):\n\n```\neffective_interval : {'start_inclusive': '2026-09-14T15:00:00Z', 'end_exclusive': '2026-09-14T19:00:00Z', 'end_tolerance_seconds': 1}\ncompletion_check   : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']   (expected_funding_hours)\ninterval_hour_utc  : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']\n```\n\nA candidate that declares the interval `[15:00, 19:00)` therefore witnesses the accrual intervals `[14:00,15:00) ÔÇĞ [17:00,18:00)` ÔÇö i.e. the accrual coverage is `[start ÔêÆ 1 h, end)`: the declared window **plus one hour before its declared start**. The start hour is mandatory, not optional: deleting the 15:00 payment from that same capture refuses with \"expects payments at [15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00] ÔÇĞ carry payments at [16:00, 17:00, 18:00]\".\n\nTwo consequences the roster and the owner should see (neither is a fence hole ÔÇö both fail toward refusal ÔÇö so neither blocks this candidate):\n\n1. `interval_hour_utc` and `effective_interval` name a **payment-stamp** window while reading as an accrual window, and the witness silently reaches one hour before the declared start. Under D-3 the owner ruled the *value* (the floor of the stamp); the *meaning* of the window relative to accrual is unruled and stated nowhere in the artifacts. It needs one owner sentence. ÔåÆ **NIT-6**.\n2. On the end side this interacts with the capture tool. r1's manifest requests `userFunding` with `endTime = 1789412400000` (= `19:00:00.000Z`), while the exporter's grid expects a payment at `19:00` whenever the position is still open then ÔÇö and that payment is stamped 41-60 ms *past* the hour, outside the capture request bounds. My D-6 (iv) mutant is exactly this case and refuses. So a real capture whose window does not end flat is, as built, structurally un-witnessable: the exporter applies the tolerance, the capture request does not. The failure is conservative (refusal, never admission), but the accepting half cannot witness the general case today. ÔåÆ **NIT-6** (same recommendation: state the semantics, and extend the capture request past the tolerance before the next capture is run).\n\n## 4. The 1-second end tolerance ÔÇö reproduced, and one thing the owner has not ruled\n\nReproduction on the r1 bytes, window `[15:00, 18:00)`, the real `18:00:00.060Z` stamp:\n\n| Stamp | Observed |\n|---|---|\n| `18:00:00.060Z` (the captured one, +0.060 s) | **accepted**, `REAL_CAPTURE_CANDIDATE_BUILT` |\n| +0.999 s | accepted |\n| **+1.000 s** | **refused** `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n| +1.060 s | refused `CANDIDATE_BINDING_OUT_OF_INTERVAL` |\n\n`end_limit = (end.seconds + 1, end.fraction)` with a strict `<` (`:1607`, `:1614`), so the admitted band is the half-open `[end, end+1 s)`. A stamp at exactly one second past the end is refused. The owner wrote \"a 1-second end-boundary tolerance\"; half-open is a defensible reading, but the boundary itself was chosen by the implementation, not by the row. ÔåÆ **NIT-2**.\n\n**The grid.** For `[15:00, 18:00)` the grid is `range(start, end+1h, 1h)` = `15, 16, 17, 18` (`:1237`) ÔÇö both endpoints inclusive. Combined with `position_at(hour)` using the position held *before* that hour (`:1222-1235`, `fill_ms < time_ms`), the grid is consistent with the venue's convention that the payment stamped at hour *H* settles `[HÔêÆ1h, H)`. Including the end hour is exactly what the owner's tolerance is for, and I confirm it is the same one second, not a second mechanism.\n\n**The start side is NOT stated anywhere, and it is not the owner's decision.** I searched all four files for any statement of which accrual interval a payment settles: the only occurrence is a test docstring, `tests/test_mtc_funding_export_real_capture.py:744` (\"the 18:00:00.060Z payment settles the 17-18 interval\"). Nothing in the exporter, the adapter, the candidate artifact or the report says it. I built the demonstrating case (position already open at the window start, payments at 15/16/17/18):\n\n```\neffective_interval : {'start_inclusive': '2026-09-14T15:00:00Z', 'end_exclusive': '2026-09-14T19:00:00Z', 'end_tolerance_seconds': 1}\ncompletion_check   : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']   (expected_funding_hours)\ninterval_hour_utc  : ['15:00', '16:00', '17:00', '18:00']\n```\n\nA candidate that declares the interval `[15:00, 19:00)` therefore witnesses the accrual intervals `[14:00,15:00) ÔÇĞ [17:00,18:00)` ÔÇö i.e. the accrual coverage is `[start ÔêÆ 1 h, end)`: the declared window **plus one hour before its declared start**. The start hour is mandatory, not optional: deleting the 15:00 payment from that same capture refuses with \"expects payments at [15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00] ÔÇĞ carry payments at [16:00, 17:00, 18:00]\".\n\nTwo consequences the roster and the owner should see (neither is a fence hole ÔÇö both fail toward refusal ÔÇö so neither blocks this candidate):\n\n1. `interval_hour_utc` and `effective_interval` name a **payment-stamp** window while reading as an accrual window, and the witness silently reaches one hour before the declared start. Under D-3 the owner ruled the *value* (the floor of the stamp); the *meaning* of the window relative to accrual is unruled and stated nowhere in the artifacts. It needs one owner sentence. ÔåÆ **NIT-6**.\n2. On the end side this interacts with the capture tool. r1's manifest requests `userFunding` with `endTime = 1789412400000` (= `19:00:00.000Z`), while the exporter's grid expects a payment at `19:00` whenever the position is still open then ÔÇö and that payment is stamped 41-60 ms *past* the hour, outside the capture request bounds. My D-6 (iv) mutant is exactly this case and refuses. So a real capture whose window does not end flat is, as built, structurally un-witnessable: the exporter applies the tolerance, the capture request does not. The failure is conservative (refusal, never admission), but the accepting half cannot witness the general case today. ÔåÆ **NIT-6** (same recommendation: state the semantics, and extend the capture request past the tolerance before the next capture is run).\n\n## 4.
